draft_role: Root reviewed actual source/code hashes, five selected final checkpoints and private HF coverage, recursive raw metric projection, native and finite-policy CPU commands, failed policy outcomes, GSM human-target segmentation and MIT notices. Original Chen2021v2 Eq1 and OpenAI implementation were additionally read to correct the n=k pass@k nuance. Actual public export and CPU checks remain separate release gates.

model_card.summary: Matched direct/visible-step TinyLMs, strict/proxy-reward finite policies and a separate human-target GSM8K loss pilot.
model_card.scope: Compare matched fresh direct-answer and visible-step TinyLMs on two-addition arithmetic, actual N-candidate selection, separate strict/proxy-reward finite policies and an independent human-target GSM8K loss pilot.
limitations: Direct and step models start from identical random weights and receive equal optimizer steps and sampled example counts, not equal supervised-token budgets.
Each N budget really samples a separate batch; candidate generations and measured batch times are preserved.
Oracle coverage is scored using known arithmetic answers; it is not a deployable general selector.
The step verifier checks both equations, linking, original operands, and final answer in this narrow task.
Visible valid steps and self-consistency do not establish faithfulness of an internal chain of thought.
Weak arithmetic generalization or GSM8K loss reduction must not be presented as natural-language complex reasoning.
These selected branches initialize fresh models in their actual code; a plan-level sft dependency is not evidence of using SFT or UltraChat weights.
This REINFORCE updates a finite 17-action policy, not the language models above.
An enumeration action exposes reward hacking in the weak any-number parser; it is never counted as a strict correct answer.
Sampled actions and token counts have different units; this policy generates zero autoregressive tokens.
All 200 original records are preserved; family splitting happens before context-reset segmentation.
All human answer target tokens occur once in the segment dataset; question-only chunks have no supervised target and are omitted.
Context resets inside long records make this a loss/dataflow pilot, not a GSM8K benchmark or demonstrated complex reasoning.
The continuation prompts expose human-answer prefixes and are explicitly excluded from answer-accuracy scoring.

N=1/2/4/8 oracle coverage is measured from independently sampled candidate batches at temperature 0.7; these are observed any-correct proportions, recorded as oracle coverage, not an equal-token-budget comparison or a HumanEval benchmark score. When n=k, the standard pass@k estimator reduces to the same any-success indicator; this run does not estimate multiple k from a larger-n sample pool. The GSM8K checkpoint is a separate width32, one-layer human-target loss pilot; its continuation prompt exposes part of the human answer.

For direct answers the reported verifier selects a candidate only after comparing it to the known gold sum, so its accuracy equals oracle coverage by construction. The visible-step verifier is a separate narrow arithmetic check of equations, linkage, original operands and final sum; neither is a general-purpose learned verifier.

The direct and visible-step language models each receive 900 updates but respectively 48803 and 466322 supervised targets. At N=1/2/4/8 the direct oracle counts are 1/1/2/1 out of 24, and step-model counts are 11/13/13/14; these are separate stochastic batches, not nested candidates or evidence that increasing N always improves this run.

Strict-reward finite-policy training reduces held-out greedy accuracy from 1/24 to 0/24 and sampled strict accuracy from 23/384 to 0/384. Weak-proxy training gives 384/384 proxy reward by selecting the enumeration action on all 384 samples, while strict correctness remains 0/384. Neither final policy demonstrates successful held-out arithmetic learning.

GSM8K validation/test are custom 20/20-record splits of the original first 200 training records, not the upstream benchmark test set. Its 150 updates consume 216776 sampled answer targets from 528 training segments containing 47486 unique targets; validation/test each contain 65 supervised segments and 5477/5931 targets. The final test NLL is 2.6746503244341175, with no problem-solving accuracy score.

inference.method: Run the three native language checkpoints with the existing CPU CLI, and the two custom finite policies with the existing eval()+no_grad() component probe. Use installed Python from the project root.
inference.scope: Load/forward/generation operation examples only. Arithmetic commands are greedy, unlike the report's sampled N-candidate evaluation. The GSM command uses an empty answer prefix for smoke checking; report continuations instead expose 40 bytes of separately sourced held-out human answers and are not problem-solving scores.

policy-strict.pt.method: Construct scripts.course_experiments.applications._FinitePolicy() on CPU; load saved["model"] strictly; call model.eval(); under torch.no_grad(), feed three six-way one-hot operands; argmax indexes architecture.actions. This finite policy generates no autoregressive tokens.
policy-strict.pt.scope: CPU load/forward component smoke check on generated input only; not a task-quality or calibration evaluation.

policy-weak_proxy.pt.method: Construct scripts.course_experiments.applications._FinitePolicy() on CPU; load saved["model"] strictly; call model.eval(); under torch.no_grad(), feed three six-way one-hot operands; argmax indexes architecture.actions. This finite policy generates no autoregressive tokens.
policy-weak_proxy.pt.scope: CPU load/forward component smoke check on generated input only; not a task-quality or calibration evaluation.

gsm8k-pilot.pt.scope: Empty answer prefix for load/generation smoke only; the report's continuation protocol supplies a held-out original human-answer prefix, not an independently solved question.
